 Firoj Khan, Resident of Habibpur, P.S. Habibpur, District - Bhagalpur.

 Appearance :
 For the Appellant : Mr. N.K. Agarwal, Sr Advocate and Mr. P  Kumar Sinha, Advocate  For the Respondent : Mr. Abhimanyu Sharma, A.P.P.
 ======================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE ANIL KUMAR SINHA  and  HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE CHANDRA PRAKASH  SINGH  ORAL ORDER  (Per: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE ANIL KUMAR SINHA)
Re. : I.A. No. 01 of 2024:
Heard learned senior counsel for the appellant and learned A.P.P. for the State.
2. The aforesaid Interlocutory Application has been filed on behalf of the sole appellant for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to him.

3. The appellant has been convicted and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for twelve years and fine of Rs. 25,000/- and in default of payment of fine, he has further been sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for three months for the offence punishable under Section 376 of the I.P.C.
He has Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.139 of 2020(9) dt.10-01-2025 further been convicted and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for twelve years and fine of Rs.

sentences.text: All the sentences have been directed to run concurrently.

4. The prosecution case, in brief, is that on 11.04.2016 at 6.45 P.M., while the informant who is the minor victim girl was going to bring Sprite at some distance from her house near 'Ansari Tea Shop',
where the appellant was present who told her to come to him alongwith him and by another hand he closed her mouth and took her in a half built house and there he put her on surface and opened her leggings and forcibly raped her which resulted in bleeding in her private part and she became senseless.

After sometime, when she gained her senses, she came to her house slowly and informed her mother and other persons about the occurrence on which her mother and family members took her to the police station.

5. Learned senior counsel for the appellant submits that during the pendency of the trial, the appellant has remained in custody from 12.04.2016 to 10.09.2016 and after pronouncement of judgment, he was taken into custody on Patna High Court CR.

APP (DB) No.139 of 2020(9)
dt.10-01-2025 10.12.2019 and since then he is in custody.

It is further submitted that the appellant has remained in custody for approximately more than five years and six months and there is no likelihood of the appeal being taken up for hearing in near future.
The victim girl in her statement recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C., has not named the appellant.
There is no compliance of Section 34(2) of the POCSO Act in the present case in light of the judgment rendered in the case of Jarnail Singh Vs. State of Haryana, reported in 2013(7)SCC 263.

entities.text: Jarnail Singh Vs. State of Haryana, reported in 2013(7)SCC 263
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has further been pointed out by learned senior counsel for the appellant that there is no statutory compliance of Sections 53A and 164A of the Cr.P.C.
It is further submitted that the P.Ws. 1 to 5 are the informant, her mother, father and brother and no independent or local witnesses were examined either by the I.O. or by the informant herself.
The final form was submitted on 30.11.2017 and after seven months, she filed this false case.
The learned court below has not considered this fact that the informant in her statement recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C., has not named the appellant.

The doctor has failed to appreciate the medical report in which spermatozoa was not found which go to suggest that the rape was not committed with the informant but since the informant was aged about 18 years Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.139 of 2020(9) dt.10-01-2025 was in habit of sexual intercourse by others.
6.
Learned A.P.P. for the State has opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the appellant and argued that the appellant is named in the F.I.R.
There is specific allegation of commission of rape upon a minor girl aged about 13 years against the appellant.
The victim girl was examined by the doctor (P.W.6) and the doctor has opined that the victim girl has been raped.
7. The bail application of the appellant was earlier rejected on 13.07.2023 by this Court on merit.

8. Regard being had to the submissions of the parties and taking into consideration the nature of allegation and the evidence adduced in the court below and the statement of the victim (P.W. 1) and bail application of the appellant was earlier rejected on its merit, we are not inclined to suspend the sentence and grant bail to the appellant at this stage, however, the appellant may renew his prayer for bail after six months in custody if the appeal is not taken up for hearing.
